flags.text: -63% of 5-yr profit turned into operating cash
Working-capital cycle lengthened 70 days in 2 yrs (now 193)

business.whatItDoes: Kaynes Technology India Limited is a vertically integrated Electronic System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) enterprise. It provides conceptual design, process engineering, component manufacturing, semiconductor packaging, and life-cycle support for mission-critical electronics.

segments.name: Industrial and EV Automotive
segments.comment: Focuses on automotive electronic control units and smart energy systems.

segments.name: IoT/IT, Consumer and Others
segments.comment: Includes high-performance computing servers and connected IoT devices.

segments.name: Railways
segments.comment: Develops signalling, rolling stock electronics, and the Kavach anti-collision system.

segments.name: Medical
segments.comment: Manufactures precision-critical diagnostic, monitoring, and healthcare electronics.

segments.name: Aerospace, Space and Outer Space, and Strategic Electronics
segments.comment: Delivers high-reliability electronics meeting stringent defence and space standards.

business.geography: Domestic and export mix is supported by manufacturing footprint expansion in India, North America via August Electronics in Canada, and Europe via Sensonic GmbH in Austria.
scale: Order book of ₹83,663 Mn as of 31 March 2026
Market capitalisation of ₹2,29,90,20,49,358 as on 31 March 2026
Consolidated revenue of ₹36,264 Mn in FY 2025-26
Workforce of 811 permanent employees and 1,713 permanent workers
risks: Geopolitical volatility, trade barriers, and component sourcing disruptions.
Working capital intensity leading to high inventory and receivable levels.
Cybersecurity risks and potential data breaches across automated systems.
Regulatory and compliance dependencies on government schemes like the ISM and PLI.

guidance.statement: We are targeting INR450 to INR500 crores full year revenue between OSAT and PCB.
guidance.quote: and we have committed a full year revenue of totally INR500 crores between both, INR450 to INR500 crores, which is what we are targeting at this point in time, we are on the target.
guidance.speaker: N. Muthukumar

growthCommentary: Total revenue grew 40% year-on-year to INR946 crores, largely driven by EMS business.
Standalone EMS business grew 53% from INR480 crores to INR639 crores.
Smart metering business saw flat to negative growth of minus 12% due to working capital constraints and flood impacts.
Overseas entities grew 327% from INR24 crores to INR102 crores due to the August Electronics acquisition.

pushback.question: Are there any thought processes to divest the metering business to release working capital and management bandwidth?
pushback.answer: Management is seriously looking at options and opportunities to de-risk receivables and will update by February.

pushback.topic: Margin Pressure and Component Cost Inflation
pushback.question: Will gross margins compress in the coming 9 months due to component shortages and price increases?
pushback.answer: Management acknowledged it is a difficult year with pricing and availability pressures, though order pricing is generally pass-on.

pushback.topic: Working Capital and Negative Cash Flow
pushback.question: How did the cash flow from operations turn out, given the negative CFO and inventory build-up?
pushback.answer: Operating cash flow was negative INR259 crores, driven by inventory addition of INR177 crores and metering receivables.

guidance.statement: Outgrow the market and double the market growth rate
guidance.quote: we chose to say this time that we'll be outgrowing the market and we'll be doubling the market growth
guidance.speaker: N. Muthukumar

guidance.statement: Rail business to grow by around 20% to 25% this year
guidance.quote: rail business, I'm expecting this year to grow by around 20%, 25% because of these coming in.
guidance.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan

guidance.statement: Do a PCB revenue of around INR300 crores to INR400 crores
guidance.quote: we will do a good number of PCB of around INR300 crores to INR400 crores
guidance.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan

guidance.statement: Do an OSAT revenue of around INR250 crores to INR300 crores
guidance.quote: and OSAT of around INR250 crores to INR300 crores.
guidance.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan

growthCommentary: Total revenue stood at INR3,626.4 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 33.2%.
Near-term top line performance missed expectations due to geopolitical disruptions, specifically the West Asia conflict leading to customer deferments and supply chain delays.
Growth was broad-based across automotive, EV, industrial, aerospace, and railway segments.
Mysore facility crossed INR10,000 million in revenue.

pushback.question: How should investors look at guidance given the vast variance between expected and delivered numbers?
pushback.answer: Management explained that aggressive targets were set based on vehicle electrification and government projects, but unexpected delays and a 90% production drop by a major 2-wheeler EV OEM caused the shortfall, assuring that orders are delayed, not canceled.

pushback.topic: Negative Operating Cash Flow / Working Capital
pushback.question: Why did operating cash flows turn deeply negative despite prior guidance of a neutral or slight negative stance?
pushback.answer: Management clarified that the core EMS business actually generated positive cash flow of INR250 crores, but the consolidated cash flow and receivables were dragged down by the newly acquired smart metering business due to slow site installation and government execution delays.

pushback.question: Why have receivables in the metering subsidiary continued to balloon without substantial collection progress?
pushback.answer: Management stated that execution of erection and commissioning in rural towns faced ground-level delays, but expects the situation to reverse and normalize within the next three quarters of the year.

guidance.statement: Aiming to achieve USD 1 billion in revenue by FY28.
guidance.quote: See, on the growth, what we have projected $1 billion, we are still sticking on to that
guidance.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan

guidance.statement: Expecting net working capital days between 70 to 85 days.
guidance.quote: So typically, what we expect is about between 70 to 85 days. Last year, it was 85 days.
guidance.speaker: Jairam Sampath

guidance.statement: Expecting at least INR1,500 crores from the OSAT business.
guidance.quote: So, at the minimum, you can expect INR1,500 crores from our OSAT business.
guidance.speaker: Jairam Sampath

guidance.statement: Expecting about INR1,000 crores from the PC Board business.
guidance.quote: Similarly, you can expect about INR1,000 crores from PC Board business.
guidance.speaker: Jairam Sampath

growthCommentary: Total revenue for the 9-month period ended December '25 stood at INR23,837 million, a 37% year-on-year growth.
Operational EBITDA for 9 months reached INR3,778 million with a margin expansion of 190 basis points to 15.9%.
Profit after tax came in at INR2,726 million, representing an 11.4% PAT margin.
Growth was impacted by temporary deferrals and delays in certain project execution such as railways Kavach.

pushback.question: The gap in terms of execution seems to have widened a bit in terms of growth in revenues despite good order inflows. How long does the current order book get executed?
pushback.answer: Customers hold inventories when projects face alignment problems, and some agencies have not yet provided approvals for deliveries.

pushback.question: Working capital was elevated sequentially by about 23 days higher compared to September '25. What is the reason and steps to bring it down?
pushback.answer: Bespoke orders require material acquisitions ahead of time. Net working capital days will improve in Q4 due to higher throughput and supply chain finance.

pushback.question: What is being done to reduce long-term debtors from the metering business carried forward from Iskraemeco?
pushback.answer: Identifying a bank for funding annuity payments sitting in noncurrent assets and converting future metering into a device business model.

growthCommentary: Growth in other verticals like automotive, industrial, EV, railways, and aerospace compensates for smart metering composition.
Smart metering business operates as a run-rate business driven by the government's RDSS program.
Other businesses besides Iskraemeco are showing strong growth rates, slightly higher than the company's total growth rate.
Commercial production for OSAT has started with sample shipments to three clients (Alpha Omega Semiconductor, Infineon, and L&T's Fujitsu General semiconductor business).

pushback.topic: Iskraemeco financials, margins, and acquisition accounting
pushback.question: Analysts questioned high H2 FY25 net margins, first-half losses reconciled with full-year profit, short payback period, and ambiguous goodwill recognition.
pushback.answer: Management stated H2 net margin was actually 9%, H1 loss was due to lower revenue, inventory write-offs, and corporate cleanup, and acquisition accounting followed Ind AS 103 using identifiable intangible assets.

pushback.topic: Working capital, cash conversion cycle, and cash flows
pushback.question: Analysts raised concerns over rising cash conversion cycles, negative operating cash flow post-interest, high capex, and discrepancies between cash flow statements and asset additions.
pushback.answer: Management explained that EMS working capital intensity is typical, supply chain finance and foreign bank discounting lower interest impacts, and cash flow purchase of fixed assets includes ROU assets net of subsidy.

pushback.topic: Related party disclosures and contingent liabilities
pushback.question: Analysts pointed out inconsistent related party transaction disclosures and an increase in contingent liabilities due to bank and corporate guarantees.
pushback.answer: Management clarified that a typographical omission in stand-alone notes to accounts caused the RPT disclosure miss, which has been rectified, and contingent liabilities reflect necessary performance and corporate guarantees for subsidiaries.

synthesis.take: While Kaynes maintains revenue growth of 40.6% YoY in Q1 FY27, net profit fell 25.3% and operating cash flow remains deeply negative. Stretched working capital cycles and execution delays in smart metering create severe cash burn that offsets order book expansion.

Achieve at least INR 1,500 crores from OSAT business
Rail business to grow by around 20% to 25%

narrative.claim: Core EMS generates positive cash flow while smart metering causes consolidated cash deficits
narrative.numbers: Consolidated CFO fell to negative ₹600 crore in FY26 and negative ₹259 crore in Q1 FY27

narrative.claim: Strong execution across industrial, automotive, and railway verticals supports sustainable earnings expansion
narrative.numbers: Q1 FY27 PAT fell 25.3% YoY to ₹56 crore despite revenue growing 40.6%

narrative.claim: Working capital days would stabilize between 70 to 85 days
narrative.numbers: Working capital days expanded to 133 days while cash conversion cycle reached 193 days

bull.point: Revenue increased 40.6% YoY to ₹946 crore in Q1 FY27, backed by an ₹83,663 million order book.
Standalone EMS grew 53% YoY, and commercial OSAT production commenced sample shipments to three international customers.
International manufacturing footprint expanded through acquisitions including August Electronics in Canada and Sensonic GmbH in Austria.

bear.point: Cash generation is deeply impaired: FY26 CFO hit -₹600 crore and 5-year profit-to-operating-cash conversion stands at -63%.
Working capital cycle lengthened significantly, with debtor days doubling to 154 days and working capital days reaching 133.
Net profit fell 25.3% YoY in Q1 FY27 and 21.6% in Q4 FY26, showing persistent margin strain.
Smart metering subsidiary suffers severe cash flow drag and high receivables due to ground-level installation delays.

watch: Reversal of negative operating cash flows and inventory additions.
Smart metering receivable recoveries or updates on potential business divestment.
Execution toward the lowered INR 450-500 crore OSAT and PCB target.
